chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man has a slave girl for one of his sons, and his son is young.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for him to sleep with her until he appraises her at a just price, then takes her, and the price remains due upon him for his son.'

key_terms.قِيمَةَ عَدْلٍ: A just price / fair market value
key_terms.يَطَأَهَا: To sleep with her / consummate marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father wants his young son to marry a slave girl owned by the son?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the legal mechanism of 'Iqat' (manumission or transfer of ownership) where a father purchases his son's slave girl to facilitate marriage, ensuring the son retains financial rights. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the son holds independent ownership of the slave, requiring the father to pay a just valuation ('qiyamat 'adl') before consummation, thereby preventing unilateral appropriation of the child's property.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Sirhan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, a man, there happens to be a slave girl for one of his son, and his son is young. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not correct that he sleeps with her until he evaluates her with a just price, then takes her, and there would happen to be upon him, for his son, its price’.
